title: Set Up Mozilla Thunderbird
cardText: Set up IMAP or POP email accounts in Mozilla Thunderbird.
Configure incoming and outgoing servers, SMTP authentication and POP message retention.
Synchronise IMAP mail or safely migrate local POP messages, Thunderbird profiles and MBOX or EML archives.
text: This guide covers Thunderbird email setup on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Use automatic account configuration where supported, or manually enter the email provider's settings.
IMAP normally restores server-stored messages and folders without importing old mail.
Check for Local Folders, POP messages and other data that will not be restored through IMAP synchronisation.
Use Thunderbird's built-in Import and Export tools for supported profile migrations.
ImportExportTools NG is an optional extension for additional MBOX, EML and other import or export operations.
When transferring old messages, use separate local staging folders and check for duplicates before merging.
Preserve the original email profile and backups until the migration has been verified.

identifySetupType.title: Identify the setup or migration
body: Determine whether Thunderbird is being configured for a new mailbox or replacing an existing email installation.
For an existing account, identify whether it uses IMAP, POP or another connection type.
IMAP normally synchronises server-stored mail and folders.
POP messages and Thunderbird Local Folders may exist only on the original computer.
If local data must be transferred, preserve the source before making changes.

identifyExistingClient.title: Identify the original email application
body: Determine whether the existing mail is stored in Thunderbird, Outlook, Apple Mail or another application.
If the source is Thunderbird, check whether its entire profile should be moved or only selected messages are needed.
A Thunderbird profile may contain accounts, local mail, address books, filters and other settings.
If the original client is different, identify its supported export or backup format.
Check for POP messages and local folders absent from webmail.
Preserve the original installation until the destination has been verified.

checkThunderbirdProfile.title: Locate the existing Thunderbird profile
body: Open Thunderbird on the original computer.
Open the application menu, Help, Troubleshooting Information.
Find Profile Folder and select Open Folder, Open Directory or Show in Finder.
The profile contains Thunderbird account settings and locally stored data.
On Windows, profiles are commonly located under %APPDATA%\Thunderbird\Profiles.
Use Thunderbird's actual profile location on macOS and Linux.
Check whether multiple profiles exist.
Close Thunderbird before copying profile files manually.

profileRecoveryRequired.title: Locate the original Thunderbird profile
body: The original Thunderbird profile has not been located.
Check Troubleshooting Information and any additional Thunderbird profiles.
On Windows, inspect the user's roaming application data folder.
Check existing computer backups and previous profile locations.
Do not remove the original installation or overwrite possible recovery data.
Continue once the required profile or mail backup is available.

link.name: Mozilla: Thunderbird Profile Locations
link.description: Official instructions for locating Thunderbird data.

exportThunderbirdProfile.title: Back up the Thunderbird profile
body: On the original computer, open Thunderbird's application menu, Tools, Export.
For profiles within the supported 2 GB ZIP export limit, use Export to create a backup ZIP.
Save the exported ZIP outside the original Thunderbird profile.
For larger profiles, locate the profile folder, close Thunderbird and make a manual backup.
When manually backing up, preserve the complete Thunderbird data structure needed for restoration.
Check that mail folders, account data and other required settings are included.
Keep an untouched backup separate from the working migration copy.
Confirm the backup is accessible before continuing.

link.description: Official instructions for manual profile backup and transfer.

exportThunderbirdProfile.alt: Thunderbird Export tool showing the profile export controls
exportThunderbirdProfile.caption: Use Thunderbird's Export tool for supported profile sizes, or manually back up larger profiles with Thunderbird closed.

backupOtherClientMail.title: Back up mail from the original application
body: Identify the original email application's storage format.
For classic Outlook, locate PST files containing POP mail and local archives.
For Apple Mail, use its supported mailbox export procedure where appropriate.
Check whether the source can export mail in MBOX or EML format.
Verify whether important messages exist on the server or only in local storage.
Preserve an untouched backup of the original messages.
Do not remove the old email installation before the backup is verified.

link.name: Microsoft: Export Outlook Mail
link.description: Official instructions for exporting messages to PST.

link.name: Mozilla: Thunderbird Import
link.description: Official information about supported import sources.

protectOriginalMail.title: Protect the original mail data
body: The original email profile or archive has not been backed up successfully.
Preserve the source computer and email application.
Check locally stored Inbox, Sent, Archive and custom folders.
Keep an untouched copy of the required profile or export files.
Do not remove accounts, delete profiles or overwrite existing mail.
Resume migration after verifying the backup.

chooseMigrationMethod.title: Choose a Thunderbird migration method
body: Determine whether the entire Thunderbird profile should be moved to a replacement installation.
Full-profile restoration is useful when transferring existing accounts, mail, address books and settings together.
A profile restore is not the same as importing a few old messages into an existing configured account.
Restoring a full profile may replace destination settings and mail data.
If Thunderbird is already configured and only some local messages are needed, prefer a selected-mail import.
Do not restore an old full profile over a working destination profile without protecting the destination first.

checkDestinationProfile.title: Check the destination Thunderbird profile
body: Determine whether the destination already contains accounts, messages or settings that must be retained.
A full-profile restore should normally use a fresh or deliberately chosen destination profile.
If Thunderbird already contains important data, back up that destination profile first.
Do not assume the Import tool will merge two complete profiles without conflicts or duplicate data.
Use selected-mail import instead if the goal is to combine messages with an existing Thunderbird installation.

restoreThunderbirdProfile.title: Restore Thunderbird on another computer
body: Install a compatible Thunderbird version on the destination computer.
Back up any existing destination profile before making changes.
For a supported Thunderbird Export ZIP, open the application menu, Tools, Import.
Choose the appropriate Thunderbird profile import source and follow the wizard.
For larger profiles, use a supported folder-based import or Mozilla's manual profile transfer procedure.
Do not copy old profile files over an active Thunderbird profile while Thunderbird is running.
Restart Thunderbird and check account settings, Local Folders, contacts and other data.
Some passwords or provider authentication approvals may need to be entered again.
Allow IMAP accounts to reconnect and synchronise normally.
Do not separately import the same message archive again without checking whether the restored profile already contains it.

link.name: Mozilla: Import Thunderbird Profile
link.description: Official built-in profile import instructions.

link.name: Mozilla: Move Thunderbird to Another Computer
link.description: Official manual profile transfer procedure.

verifyRestoredProfile.title: Verify the restored Thunderbird profile
body: Check the restored accounts and their connection settings.
Verify that required POP messages and Local Folders are accessible.
Check address books, filters and other settings that formed part of the profile.
For IMAP, allow normal server synchronisation and compare important folders with webmail.
Check whether messages appear twice or additional source archives remain unimported.
If required mail is present and the profile works, no separate message import is needed.
If the restored profile is incomplete, preserve its backup and investigate the missing data.

collectAccountDetails.title: Identify the account and provider settings
body: Obtain the complete email address and supported authentication method.
Determine whether the mailbox requires IMAP or POP.
For manual setup, obtain incoming and SMTP server names, ports and encryption.
Check whether the provider requires OAuth or an app-specific password.
Confirm that IMAP or POP is enabled by the provider.
Use the provider's current documentation rather than guessing settings.

link.name: Mozilla: Automatic Account Configuration
link.description: Official instructions for automatic mailbox setup.

link.name: Mozilla: Manual Account Configuration
link.description: Official instructions for entering mail server settings.

obtainProviderSettings.title: Obtain the provider configuration
body: The required incoming or outgoing account settings are unavailable.
Check the provider's official Thunderbird setup documentation.
Record the protocol, server names, ports, encryption and authentication requirements.
Check whether the provider permits the selected connection type.
Do not disable encryption or use insecure authentication to force the connection.
Continue once the correct settings are available.

addEmailAccount.title: Add an email account in Thunderbird
body: Open Mozilla Thunderbird.
On a new installation, use the existing email account setup screen.
On an installed system, open the application menu, New Account, Existing Email, where available.
Enter the display name and complete email address.
Enter the account password when required.
Select Continue to detect the available provider configuration.
Review the incoming and outgoing settings.
Complete any required browser-based provider authentication.

link.name: Mozilla: Add an Existing Email Account
link.description: Official Thunderbird automatic setup instructions.

chooseProtocol.title: Choose IMAP or POP
body: Review the account configurations detected by Thunderbird.
Choose IMAP when messages and folders should synchronise across devices.
Choose POP when the required configuration downloads incoming messages for primarily local storage.
POP cannot restore messages previously removed from the server by another computer.
An existing IMAP account cannot simply be converted into POP; a separate account configuration is required.
Check that the provider supports the selected protocol.
If the detected settings are unsuitable, choose manual configuration.

link.description: Official explanation of IMAP and POP selection.

link.name: Mozilla: Change from IMAP to POP
link.description: Official guidance on setting up a separate POP account.

chooseProtocol.alt: Thunderbird account setup screen showing IMAP and POP3 options
chooseProtocol.caption: Choose IMAP for synchronised mail or POP3 when a local-download configuration is required.

manualAccountSetup.title: Configure incoming and outgoing servers manually
body: In the account setup window, select Configure manually or Manual config.
Enter the incoming server hostname supplied by the email provider.
Select IMAP or POP3 as the incoming protocol.
Enter the required incoming port, connection security and authentication method.
Enter the outgoing SMTP hostname, port and encryption.
Enter the required incoming and outgoing usernames.
Common encrypted incoming ports are 993 for IMAP and 995 for POP.
Common SMTP submission ports are 587 with STARTTLS and 465 with SSL/TLS.
Use the provider's documented settings if they differ.
Select Re-test where available before completing setup.

link.name: Mozilla: Manual Account Configuration
link.description: Official Thunderbird manual server setup instructions.

configureImap.title: Complete the IMAP account setup
body: Confirm the incoming IMAP server, port and encryption.
Use the provider's required username and authentication method.
Check the outgoing SMTP configuration.
Complete any OAuth or multifactor authentication prompts.
Select Done when Thunderbird confirms the configuration.
Allow Thunderbird to retrieve the server mailbox folders.
Do not import an old local archive before checking whether the required messages are already on the server.

link.name: Mozilla: Manual IMAP Configuration
link.description: Official instructions for configuring Thunderbird IMAP.

configurePop.title: Complete the POP account setup
body: Confirm that POP3 is selected as the incoming protocol.
Enter the provider's POP server hostname and required username.
Use the documented port and encryption, commonly 995 with SSL/TLS.
Check outgoing SMTP server settings.
Complete provider authentication and select Done.
Confirm the POP account appears in Thunderbird.
Before downloading a large existing mailbox, review server retention.
Keep the original POP profile or local archive backed up.
Do not assume previously downloaded messages will automatically reappear.

link.name: Mozilla: POP Configuration
link.description: Official guidance for configuring POP in Thunderbird.

configurePopRetention.title: Check POP message retention
body: Open Thunderbird Account Settings.
Select the POP account and open Server Settings.
Review Leave messages on server.
Check options for deleting server copies after a set number of days or when deleted locally.
When migrating between two computers, retaining messages temporarily can help prevent premature server deletion.
Check the provider's mailbox storage limit.
Choose a retention policy suitable for the user's requirements.
Preserve the original local POP messages and verify that new messages download correctly.

link.name: Mozilla: POP Account Setup
link.description: Official Thunderbird POP setup information.

link.name: Mozilla Support: POP Retention
link.description: Information about Leave messages on server.

checkSmtp.title: Verify outgoing SMTP configuration
body: Open Account Settings and select Outgoing Server (SMTP).
Confirm that the correct SMTP server is associated with the email account.
Check the server hostname, port, encryption and authentication method.
Use OAuth where supported and required by the provider.
Do not disable encryption to work around sign-in errors.
Save the settings and proceed with a sending and receiving test.

link.name: Mozilla: Manual Account Configuration
link.description: Official instructions for outgoing SMTP settings.

testEmail.title: Test sending and receiving
body: Send a plain test message to another accessible email address.
Reply from that address and confirm the response arrives.
Check the message appears in the expected Sent folder.
Check for connection or authentication errors.
For POP, verify incoming downloads and server retention.
Once sending and receiving work, identify the account protocol before deciding whether old mail must be imported.

troubleshootAccountSetup.title: Investigate Thunderbird connection errors
body: Record the exact error reported by Thunderbird.
Confirm the incoming and outgoing server names and ports.
Check whether IMAP or POP is configured correctly.
Verify the required encryption and authentication method.
Check OAuth, app-password and provider access requirements.
Compare access with webmail to identify account problems.
Correct the identified issue and test again.

link.name: Mozilla: Manual Configuration
link.description: Official Thunderbird server configuration help.

link.name: Mozilla: Thunderbird Support
link.description: Official troubleshooting information.

checkAccountSyncType.title: Identify whether the mailbox synchronises
body: Check the account's Server Settings in Thunderbird.
IMAP accounts normally synchronise messages and folders stored on the email server.
POP accounts generally download incoming mail into local storage.
For IMAP, verify normal server synchronisation before importing any previous messages.
For POP, check whether required older messages are missing from the current installation.

verifyServerSyncedMail.title: Verify IMAP messages and folders
body: Allow Thunderbird to synchronise the existing mailbox.
Compare Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Archive and custom folders with the provider's webmail.
Check older messages and attachments where available.
Expand the account's folders and check any folder subscriptions.
Some messages may not be stored for offline use even though they are available on the server.
Do not import local mail to compensate for a normal synchronisation problem.
If the server messages are present, continue to the local-only folder check.

investigateSyncMissing.title: Determine where missing IMAP messages are stored
body: Search for the missing messages in webmail.
Check Archive, Trash and any custom server folders.
If the messages are present in webmail but missing in Thunderbird, investigate synchronisation and folder visibility.
If the messages are absent from webmail but available in the old Thunderbird installation, they may be in Local Folders or another local archive.
Do not import an entire old profile until the location of the missing messages is understood.

troubleshootImapSync.title: Investigate Thunderbird IMAP synchronisation
body: Confirm Thunderbird is connected to the correct account.
Check folder subscriptions, filters and folder visibility.
Review Account Settings, Server Settings and Synchronization & Storage.
Check whether the account is offline or has authentication errors.
Allow large folders to finish synchronising.
Compare again with webmail before attempting a local mail import.

checkMissingMailSource.title: Check for missing local-only messages
body: Inspect Thunderbird Local Folders on the original computer.
Check old POP folders, archives and any additional Thunderbird profiles.
Check exported MBOX or EML files where available.
If the messages exist locally but not on the server, back up that local data before transferring it.
If the messages cannot be located locally or on the server, investigate available backups or the provider.
Avoid importing unrelated archives to solve a missing server-message problem.

checkLocalOnlyData.title: Check for local-only folders and messages
body: Inspect the original Thunderbird installation after confirming that IMAP mail has synchronised.
Check Local Folders, locally stored archives and messages downloaded under a previous POP setup.
Also check address books, calendars, filters and other settings that may need separate transfer.
IMAP does not itself synchronise Thunderbird Local Folders or local address books.
If all required mail is already on the server and there is no additional local data to transfer, no mail import is necessary.
If required local-only data exists, confirm that it has been backed up before importing it.

checkMigrationRequired.title: Check whether previous POP mail must be transferred
body: Check whether this is a replacement computer or a newly configured POP account.
Older POP messages may exist only in the original Thunderbird profile.
Check old Inbox, Sent, Archive and custom folders.
A new POP account will not automatically restore messages already removed from the server.
Compare required old mail with messages visible in the new installation.
If older local mail is needed, back it up and transfer it using the controlled migration process.

confirmLocalBackup.title: Confirm that local mail has been backed up
body: Locate the required mail in the original Thunderbird profile or another email client's archive.
Back up the original profile or exported messages.
Preserve an untouched copy of the source data.
Confirm that Inbox, Sent and any custom local folders are included.
Check that the backup files are readable.
Do not begin an import if the original local messages have not been protected.

link.name: Mozilla: Thunderbird Profile Locations
link.description: Official information about local mail storage.

link.name: Mozilla: Export Thunderbird Profile
link.description: Official export and backup procedure.

identifyMailSource.title: Identify the format of the old mail
body: Check whether the source is a Thunderbird profile, MBOX files, EML files, Outlook PST or another email application.
Thunderbird can import supported data through its built-in Import tool.
ImportExportTools NG can provide additional MBOX and EML import options.
Do not rename PST files to MBOX because changing the filename does not convert the contents.
Use the source format and intended destination to choose the migration method.

prepareLocalStaging.title: Prepare a separate local staging folder
body: In Thunderbird Local Folders, create a folder named Imported Old Mail.
For multiple archives, create clearly named subfolders identifying each source or import batch.
Import old messages into this separate local area where the chosen import tool permits it.
Do not import old messages directly into an existing IMAP Inbox or Sent folder.
Check available disk space before importing large archives.
A staging folder isolates imported mail but does not automatically remove duplicate messages.
Preserve the original source files throughout the transfer.

chooseImportMethod.title: Choose built-in Import or ImportExportTools NG
body: Use Thunderbird's built-in Tools, Import for supported profile, application and file imports.
Use ImportExportTools NG as an optional additional method for MBOX, EML or EMLX files.
For an existing Thunderbird profile, restore the entire profile only when that is the intended migration.
If only selected messages are needed, avoid replacing a working Thunderbird profile.
For MBOX and EML imports, keep the imported messages in Local Folders until they have been reviewed.
Choose the method that supports the source format without merging old mail into populated folders.

link.name: Mozilla: Thunderbird Import Tool
link.description: Official built-in mail and profile import options.

link.name: ImportExportTools NG
link.description: Optional Thunderbird extension for additional MBOX, EML and folder import or export operations.

importPreviousMail.title: Import mail using Thunderbird's built-in tool
body: Open Thunderbird's application menu, Tools, Import.
Select the supported source application, Thunderbird profile or file import option.
Review whether the operation will import individual data types or restore an entire profile.
For Outlook, Thunderbird's built-in importer may require a supported Outlook installation rather than just a standalone PST.
Select only the required mail data where the tool provides that option.
Use an isolated import destination if the available workflow supports it.
If the tool cannot keep old mail separate from populated folders, cancel and use another compatible method.
Complete the import and inspect the resulting folders.
Do not repeat a partial import without checking which messages are already present.
Keep the original backup unchanged.

link.name: Mozilla: Import into Thunderbird
link.description: Official built-in Import tool instructions.

importPreviousMail.alt: Thunderbird Import Tool showing supported application and file sources
importPreviousMail.caption: Use the built-in Import tool for supported sources, but review the import destination before combining data.

importWithImportExportToolsNg.title: Import MBOX or EML using ImportExportTools NG
body: In Thunderbird, open Add-ons and Themes.
Find ImportExportTools NG in the official Thunderbird Add-ons directory.
Check that the available extension version supports the installed Thunderbird release.
Review the extension's requested permissions before installing it.
In the folder pane, select or create an appropriate folder beneath Local Folders.
Use the ImportExportTools NG menu available from the folder context menu or Tools menu, depending on the installed version.
Choose the appropriate MBOX or EML import operation.
Select the preserved source files and import them into a separate staging folder.
For MBOX archives, preserve the original subfolder structure where supported.
Do not attempt to import an MBOX directly into an IMAP folder when the extension requires Local Folders.
Do not rename a PST or another archive format to MBOX.
After importing, inspect the messages and attachments before moving anything into a live mailbox.
Keep the source files and avoid repeating the same import until the first result is checked.

link.name: Thunderbird Add-ons: ImportExportTools NG
link.description: Official add-on listing covering MBOX, EML, EMLX, folder and profile operations.

link.name: ImportExportTools NG Source and Documentation
link.description: Project documentation, release information and usage notes.

checkPartialImport.title: Check a partial or interrupted mail import
body: Do not immediately repeat the entire import.
Inspect the destination folders to determine which messages were already transferred.
Compare imported folders, date ranges and message counts with the source.
Check for damaged archives, unsupported formats or insufficient disk space.
If using an extension, verify that it is compatible with the Thunderbird version.
Correct the problem before attempting another import.
If another attempt is required, use a newly labelled staging folder or import only missing data.
Preserve the original source files and incomplete import until the result is understood.

reviewStagedMail.title: Review imported messages for duplicates
body: Inspect the Imported Old Mail staging folder and its subfolders.
Compare the imported messages with existing local and IMAP folders.
Check sender, recipient, subject, date, contents and attachments when identifying likely duplicates.
Messages in the same conversation may share a subject without being duplicates.
Check that important older POP messages and local Sent folders are present.
Do not delete messages solely because their subjects or dates match.
For large imports, compare smaller groups before merging.
Keep uncertain messages separate rather than risking deletion of required mail.

resolveImportDuplicates.title: Resolve duplicates or missing imported messages
body: Compare suspected duplicates with messages already stored in the destination.
Check contents and attachments before treating messages as identical.
Only remove confirmed redundant staging copies when the required messages exist elsewhere.
If messages are missing, inspect the original archive or other source folders.
Do not assume ImportExportTools NG automatically prevents duplicates across existing mail folders.
Keep the original source backup unchanged.
If the result cannot be reconciled confidently, leave the imported archive separate.

checkMailDestination.title: Keep imported mail local or upload to IMAP
body: Decide whether the reviewed historical messages should remain in Thunderbird Local Folders.
Local Folders are stored on the computer and do not automatically synchronise with the email provider.
Keeping a local archive may be sufficient for old POP messages.
If the user needs the old messages on multiple devices, copy them into the configured IMAP mailbox.
Check the server mailbox quota before uploading large archives.
Do not merge unreviewed messages directly into existing IMAP folders.
Retain the original mail backup regardless of the selected destination.

uploadMailToImap.title: Copy reviewed mail into the IMAP mailbox
body: Confirm that the destination IMAP account is connected and synchronising.
Create a separate Imported Old Mail folder under that IMAP account.
Copy the reviewed messages or local archive subfolders into the separate IMAP staging location.
Use manageable batches for large message collections.
Monitor upload progress, synchronisation errors and mailbox storage.
Check webmail to confirm that the messages have reached the server.
Do not immediately copy the entire staging folder into existing Inbox or Sent folders.
Keep the original Local Folders and exported files unchanged until the upload is verified.

checkPartialUpload.title: Check an incomplete IMAP upload
body: Do not immediately repeat the entire message copy.
Compare the IMAP staging folder with the local source.
Check which messages are already visible in webmail.
Investigate mailbox quota limits, connection errors and unsupported or oversized messages.
Correct the problem and transfer only missing messages where possible.
Use a separately labelled folder for a new attempt if the previous result is uncertain.
Keep the local source and original backups.

chooseMergeMethod.title: Keep the IMAP archive separate or merge messages
body: Decide whether Imported Old Mail should remain as a separate historical folder on the IMAP server.
Keeping it separate avoids changing the existing Inbox and Sent folders.
If normal mailbox placement is required, compare the staged messages with the destination folders first.
Copy only messages confirmed to be missing.
Do not rely on Thunderbird to identify every duplicate automatically.
Keep source and staging copies until the merge has been verified.

mergeReviewedMail.title: Merge only messages missing from existing folders
body: Identify messages that do not already exist in the destination Inbox, Sent, Archive or custom folders.
Copy only the required messages from the IMAP staging folder.
Transfer smaller groups so errors or duplicate copies can be identified.
Allow Thunderbird to finish server synchronisation.
Verify the copied messages and attachments through webmail where available.
Do not delete the staging folder or source archive until the merge is complete.
If duplicate or missing messages are discovered, return to the review process.

verifyMigratedMail.title: Verify imported mail and folders
body: Compare the destination Thunderbird installation with the original profile or archive.
Check Inbox, Sent, Archive, Local Folders, Imported Old Mail and custom folders.
Open older messages and verify their attachments.
Check dates and folder organisation.
Look for unintended duplicates after any merge.
If mail was copied to IMAP, confirm the intended messages are present in webmail.
For POP, confirm the local messages remain accessible and backed up.
Check address books, filters and calendars separately if required.
Keep the original profile and archives until the migration has been verified.

migrationEscalation.title: Further Thunderbird migration required
body: The required mail could not be imported or reconciled safely.
Preserve the original Thunderbird profile and all source exports.
Keep partial imports in separate folders.
Record the Thunderbird version, source format, migration method and exact errors.
Check profile compatibility, import format, mailbox storage and synchronisation issues.
For MBOX or EML, check ImportExportTools NG compatibility and usage instructions.
For Outlook PST, determine whether a supported Outlook import or conversion workflow is available.
Do not merge uncertain messages or delete original archives.

setupComplete.title: Thunderbird email setup completed
body: The email account can send and receive messages.
Incoming and outgoing server settings are configured correctly.
For IMAP, the required server messages and folders have synchronised.
If no local-only mail is missing, no message import was necessary.
For POP, the server retention settings and local mail storage have been reviewed.
Any required previous messages or profile data have been restored, imported or retained as a verified separate archive.
Imported messages were reviewed for duplicates before merging into existing folders.
Check address books, signatures, filters and calendars separately where required.
Retain verified backups of important locally stored mail.

setupEscalation.title: Further Thunderbird account diagnostics
body: Thunderbird cannot connect to the email provider after checking protocol and account settings.
Record the Thunderbird version, provider, account type and exact error.
Confirm that the selected IMAP or POP connection and authentication method are supported.
Check OAuth, multifactor authentication and administrator-controlled restrictions.
Compare the account with the provider's webmail service.
Use the Email Not Working guide for further connection and delivery diagnostics.
Preserve any existing POP and Local Folders data while investigating.
